newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt mgrs' views unchanged w/e Mar 25 - survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt mgrs' views unchanged w/e Mar 25 - survey.

text.p: Money managers' activity was relatively subdued in U.S. debt markets last week, leaving little net change in portfolios for the second consecutive week, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"Flows were two-way, and the net result was little change in the summary structural statistics of the survey," the report said.
"There is some indication that some money managers are at least considering moving more out of the curve," it said.
In the week ended March 25, duration bogey was unchanged at 4.14 on an arithmetic basis and at 4.70 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The survey's bear/bull index fell to 4.72 from 4.76 on an arithmetic basis. It rose to 5.01 from 4.98 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio fell to 7.02 percent from 7.18 percent.
Sixteen percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, up from 12 percent the week before.
The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active rose to 5.75 from 5.33 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
